title: Fire & Smoke Mitigation Field Billing Standard: Equipment Days, Cleaning Lines and Labor
content:
## Standard

> The job must be in cleaning or cleaning complete status when an equipment day or cleaning line is charged. Equipment is billed per unit per calendar day it runs, the set and removal days each counting, up to the tier's billable equipment day cap; days beyond the cap are not billed. Ozone may be billed only on a job whose occupants are not in the structure during the work. Cleaning, demolition, sealing and labor lines are billed at the tier's unit rate times the quantity, a code whose rate is 0.00 on the tier being unavailable, and after-hours labor at the hourly rate times the after-hours labor multiplier. An odor that returns within the tier's odor recheck window after cleaning complete is rechecked and re-treated once at no charge; further rechecks, or rechecks after the window, are billed at the odor recheck fee. Lead-safe setup is billable only for housing built before the RRP year-built cutoff where painted surfaces are disturbed, following the EPA Renovation, Repair and Painting Rule, and asbestos sampling only for buildings built before the asbestos sampling cutoff, before any demolition. Amounts are rounded to the cent, half up.

This standard governs the Fire & Smoke Mitigation lines booked once cleaning has begun: air-cleaning and deodorization equipment days, and every cleaning, demolition, sealing, deodorization, handling, regulated-material and labor line.

## 1. Status

An equipment day line or a cleaning line may be charged only while the job is in cleaning or cleaning complete status. In dispatched, authorized, invoiced, closed or cancelled status neither kind of line may be charged.

## 2. Equipment days

2.1 Each unit of equipment is billed for each calendar day it runs. The day the equipment is set and the day it is removed each count as a calendar day.

2.2 A day line is the number of units running that day times the tier's daily rate for that equipment type.

2.3 The tier's billable equipment day cap limits the number of calendar days billed on the job. The days counted against the cap are the distinct calendar days on which equipment day lines are billed on the job, whatever the number of units or equipment types on each day. Days beyond the cap are not billed.

2.4 Ozone may be billed only on a job whose record shows the occupants do not stay in the structure during the work. On a job whose occupants stay in the structure, no ozone generator day is billed.

Hypothetical run: on a hypothetical tier with a cap of 4 days, an air scrubber is set on a Monday and removed on the following Saturday. Monday and Saturday both count, so the unit ran on 6 calendar days. Only 4 calendar days are billable on the job; the other 2 days are not billed. If a second air scrubber ran on two of the billed days, those days still count once each against the cap, and each of those day lines is 2 units times the daily rate.

## 3. Cleaning, demolition, sealing, handling and labor lines

3.1 Each line is the tier's unit rate for that service code times the quantity performed.

3.2 A service code whose rate on the job's tier is 0.00 is unavailable on that tier.

3.3 Labor performed after hours is billed at the hourly rate times the after-hours labor multiplier.

Hypothetical labor lines: with a hypothetical hourly rate of 80.00 and a hypothetical multiplier of 1.5, 3 business-hours hours are 3 times 80.00, which is 240.00, and 3 after-hours hours are 3 times 120.00, which is 360.00.

## 4. Odor rechecks

An odor that returns within the tier's odor recheck window after cleaning complete is rechecked and re-treated once at no charge. Further rechecks, and any recheck after the window, are billed at the tier's odor recheck fee.

| Recheck visit | Within the window after cleaning complete | After the window |
|---|---|---|
| First recheck | no charge | billed at the odor recheck fee |
| Second or later recheck | billed at the odor recheck fee | billed at the odor recheck fee |

## 5. Lead-safe setup and asbestos sampling

5.1 Lead-safe setup is billable only for housing built before the tier's RRP year-built cutoff, and only where painted surfaces are disturbed, following the EPA Renovation, Repair and Painting Rule. Housing built in the cutoff year or later does not carry lead-safe setup, nor does work that disturbs no painted surface.

5.2 Asbestos sampling is billable only for buildings built before the tier's asbestos sampling cutoff, and it is done before any demolition. A building built in the cutoff year or later does not carry asbestos sampling.

| Year built against the cutoff | Painted surfaces disturbed | Lead-safe setup billable? |
|---|---|---|
| before the RRP cutoff | yes | may be billed |
| before the RRP cutoff | no | no |
| in or after the RRP cutoff year | yes or no | no |

## 6. Rounding

Every amount under this standard is rounded to the cent, half up. A hypothetical 333 square feet at a hypothetical rate of 0.35 is 116.55; a hypothetical 12.5 square feet at a hypothetical 0.33 is 4.125, which rounds half up to 4.13.
